newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Economist upbeat on S.Africa 1997 economic outlook.
newsitem.headline: Economist upbeat on S.Africa 1997 economic outlook.

text.p: South Africa's short-term economic prospects were less gloomy than generally believed as the worst of the rand's slide was over and a rising inflation rate looked under control, a leading economist said on Tuesday.
"The short term outlook is a lot less gloomy than most imagine," said Rudolf Gouws, an economist at Rand Merchant Bank Ltd.
"The rand will not be much different at the end of this year than it is now," Gouws said addressing the 1996 South African Chamber of Business convention.
The rand was on Tuesday last trading at 4.5385 against the U.S. dollar. The local unit has lost almost a quarter of its value against the dollar since the middle of February.
"Inflation will not rise by more than 1.5 percentage points before it declines again," he said.
South Africa's consumer price index rose to a 7.5 percent year-on-year in August, its highest level in a year and its fourth consecutive monthly increase.
Money market rates were expected to hold current levels until the end of the year, falling in the course of next year.
Gouws said the economy would continue to expand next year although at a slower pace, boosted by increased export activity and a decline in imports.
"Yes, there will be a slowdown in the economy but there will still be growth. At worst it will be 2.5 percent in 1997, buoyed by growing exports and a slowdown in imports."
South Africa's economy grew by 3.3 percent in 1995.
Other factors which would boost the economy next year were an expected decrease in government spending and an environment of expanding overseas economies, Gouws said.
